analysis:
Integration review of a PR that widens inline-video handling in the provider media path (T-050, TB-003, TB-007) and updates docs and tests.

Production change, MediaIngest.swift (~769-801): decodeVideo now checks the header against the lowercased set admittedVideoDataURIHeaders (mp4, x-m4v, quicktime, mov; base64 only). The uri must still start with data:, so http(s) and file URIs are rejected. dataFromDataURI still enforces maxMediaDecodedBytes before allocation. MemoryBackedVideoAsset still sniffs the container from the bytes, so the label is not trusted. The memory-backed asset with forbidAll reference restrictions is unchanged, so no plaintext temp file is added and the T-050 mitigation holds. The duration, frame-pixel, count and aggregate caps (enforceVideoLimits) are not touched. The new labels reach only the MP4/QuickTime parser that was already reachable. The error message no longer echoes request-derived content. T-041 prefix-cache exposure is unchanged: docs state that media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture.

Docs and threat-model edits (docs/threat-model.yaml 1969-1970, inference.md, cli-reference.md line 52) match the code. They keep the caps and the rejection of http(s) and file URIs.

Tests: GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests adds an SHA-256-checked fixture and an end-to-end readiness test. MediaIngestTests adds alias tests, including rejection of non-video bytes and of non-base64 URIs.

Unverified contracts, not findings:
1. The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump (7bed8216 to 54227bab) is not visible. It carries the GLM5NextProcessor VFR frame indexing (i / nominalFrameRate) and possibly MemoryBackedVideoAsset changes. It must still enforce the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap and the 28,532 visual-token cap, and handle a zero or NaN nominalFrameRate. It must also keep the loader memory-only, with no file-URL or network fallback.
2. Whether a VFR track with many frames can bypass the frame-count or decode-work bounds before the cap is applied.
No concrete regression is established. A submodule diff review is recommended.
